To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) latency III EBV(+) Burkitt's lymphomas (BLs) are resistant to p53-induced apoptosis, (2) Bcl-2 overproduction is responsible for the resistance, (3) the Bcl- 2/Bax interaction is disrupted by a Bcl-2 homology domain 3 (BH3) mimetic, (4) Bax activation by the BH3 mimetic allows p53-induced apoptosis.
latency III EBV (−/+)-positive Burkitt's lymphomas are resistant to apoptosis induced by nutlin- 3, a small molecule that binds to the MDM2 protein and induces p53 activation.
latency III EBV(+)-infected B-cell lines are resistant to p53-mediated apoptotic cell death.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the Epstein–Barr Virus (EBV) in the development of Burkitt's lymphomas.
the development of a new therapeutic approach for EBV-associated cancers.
the role of p53 and Bcl- 2 in the resistance of latency I EBV(+) cells to apoptosis and the mechanisms of action of BH3-mimetics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the resistance of latency II and III EBV(+) cells to apoptosis is due to a selective overexpression of Bcl-2 and that the combination of a Bcl-2 antagonist (ABT-737) and a MDM2 antagonist (nutlin-3) is a potential therapeutic option for the treatment of EBV-associated cancers.
the combination of nutlin-3 and ABT-737 overcomes the resistance to p53-mediated cell death of latency III EB virus-positive cells by inducing apoptosis.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the resistance to p53-mediated cell death of BL cells harboring wild-type (wt) p53 and EBV (+) in the latency III state is due to overproduction of Bcl-2, which prevents Bax activation by the Mdm2 inhibitor nutlin-3.
the resistance to p53-induced apoptosis of EBV (+) BL cells is due to the selective overproduction of Bcl-2 and that this resistance can be overcome by a combination of MDM2 and Bcl2 inhibitors.
EBV latency III cells, which are resistant to p53-induced apoptosis, can be sensitized by ABT-737 to p53-induced cell death.
The main takeaway from our work is that
latency III Burkitt's lymphomas (BLs), which are associated with EBV infection, are resistant to apoptosis triggered by the activation of p53.
the combination of Mdm-2 inhibitors and ABT-737 is able to induce apoptosis in latency III EB virus-positive cells, a situation that occurs in Burkitt's Lymphoma.
the combination of nutlin and ABT-737 is an efficient strategy to overcome the resistance to p53-induced apoptosis of EBV (+) BL cells.
